Amina's grandmother wove carpets on a big wooden loom — a frame with threads stretched across it — in a corner of the house. Every evening Amina sat beside her, watching her fingers as she tied the knots.

One day she said, "Teach me, Grandma."
So her grandmother set up a little loom for her, gave her some red wool, and said, "One knot at a time, one row at a time. A rug isn't woven in a day."

Amina worked fast. She tied twenty knots in an hour and got up, very pleased.

Her grandmother looked at the weaving. The row was crooked and the knots were loose, so she calmly undid all of it and said, "Start again."

Amina sat down again. She tied knots and hurried, and the row went crooked a second time, and her grandmother undid it.

Amina cried and said, "I'll never learn! You weave so fast, and I can't do it."

Her grandmother went to an old chest and took out a small rug with faded colours and slightly crooked rows.

She said, "This is the first rug I ever wove, when I was your age. I wove it for a whole winter, and my mother undid it more times than I can count."
Then she said, "Speed comes from patience — not patience from speed. Ask Allah for help, count your knots, and don't look at the end of the rug."

Amina went back to her loom. Now she tied each knot and then pulled it tight, counting in a whisper, and she did not get up until the row was straight.

A single row took her a whole evening.

The winter went by like that. There was snow on the mountains, fire in the stove, and every evening the rows of red wool grew a little higher.

On some nights she got tired and left the loom, and then came back to it the next day.

When spring came, her grandmother cut the last threads, shook out the little rug, and spread it on the floor.

It was red, with straight rows, and in the middle was a little yellow star that Amina had woven all by herself.

Amina spread it in the spot where her grandmother prayed and said, "This is for you, Grandma — my first rug."

Her grandmother sat down on it and stroked the yellow star. She did not say anything, but her eyes were smiling.

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾

📖 Al-Baqarah 153. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
